item.title: Study links high-fat diet to faster breast cancer progression
item.description: If you're diagnosed with breast cancer, what should you eat to ensure the best prognosis?

item.title: Innovative peptide stapling system targets hard-to-treat cancers
item.description: Researchers at the University of Bath have developed a new technology that uses bacteria to build, chemically stabilize, and test millions of potential drug molecules inside living cells, making it much quicker and easier to discover new treatments for difficult-to-treat cancers.

item.title: Gut bacteria may explain differences in peanut allergy reactions
item.description: One of the big mysteries in food allergy is why two people with similar levels of peanut specific antibodies can react so differently. It turns out the answer may be in the mouth and gut's bacteria.

item.title: Covid lockdowns slowed executive function growth in young children
item.description: The Covid pandemic disrupted children's ability to self-regulate - according to new research from the University of East Anglia.

item.title: New strategy targets Porphyromonas gingivalis without harming healthy microbes
item.description: For years, treating gum disease has meant scraping away plaque, cutting out damaged tissue or turning to antibiotics that kill bacteria indiscriminately.

item.title: Seven hours sleep linked to lower insulin resistance risk
item.description: Sleeping for 7 hours and 18 minutes every night may be the sweet spot for warding off the risk of insulin resistance-the precursor to type 2 diabetes-suggests a large observational study published in the open access journal BMJ Open Diabetes Research & Care.

item.title: New HIV-seq tool advances understanding of persistent viral reservoirs
item.description: For people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), life-saving antiretroviral therapy keeps their HIV-infected immune cells from making new copies of the virus, preventing illness and transmission.

item.title: Alcohol-warning labels and pricing could prevent cancer deaths
item.description: If Canadian jurisdictions mandated warning labels on alcohol and minimum pricing tied to the number of standard drinks in a container, it could prevent hundreds of cancer diagnoses and deaths, according to a new study led by University of Victoria's Canadian Institute for Substance Use Research (CISUR).

item.title: Canadian wildfire pollution associated with increased stroke severity
item.description: Short-term surges in air pollution in New Jersey from the 2023 Canadian wildfires were associated with a higher stroke rate and more serious strokes, according to a preliminary study released March 3, 2026, that will be presented at the American Academy of Neurology's 78th Annual Meeting taking place April 18-22, 2026, in Chicago and online.

item.title: Ultra-processed foods linked to behavioral issues in preschoolers
item.description: A team led by researchers at the University of Toronto has found an association between ultra-processed foods in early childhood, and behavioral and emotional development.
